segments.text: Hi everyone....Im Nikki cofounder at Jexo and
Today we will learn more about value  vs effort prioritization technique.
Value vs effort model is the simplest and  quickest of all prioritization techniques.
It’s best fit for prioritising  new products or MVPs,
personal todos or small backlogs but  also for priorizing product feedback.
Given its simplicity you can  prioritise with it literary anything.
This prioritization method is pretty simple.  You need to asses two key metrics for your
priorities - value and effort....obviously... Once you fill these you can calculated the
priority score and use priority  matrix to identify quick wins.
To assign Value metric ask the question  “how does this contribute to our goal?”
And assign values from low to high.
And to fill effort metric ask “how  difficult it is to deliver the task”.
You can use T-shirt sizes for estimation, teams  are usually much more comfortable with them
because they don’t commit  to any specific timeframe.
Once you assign these metrics you can calculate  the priority score with the following formula.
However this method is much more  popular to be used together with
value versus effort priority matrix. You can simple create a chart where on x axes
you place value and on y axes effort. When you  split chart in the middle it creates quadrants.
You can then identify a low effort and high value  quadrant where you can often find a quick wins
or in other words low hanging fruit. Another useful quadrant is high
effort and low impact. Priorities in this quadrant
can be referred to as time and money sinks. Other two quadrants represent big projects - the
one with high value and high effort. And fill ins - the low value and low effort one.
As you can see when using  priority matrix it’s very easy
to identify what’s best to start  working on first and create a plan.
Now let’s have a look at the real example. I have an example backlog with tasks to
prioritise in Jira and I’m using Foxly  app for Jira to record our metrics.
First we’ll be signing value and answering  question how does this contribute to our
goal. The goal in this case is to decrease churn.  Keeping this in mind the Onboarding video brings
high value because currently we’re lacking with  our user onboarding and not enough users get to
aha moment fast enough and stop using the app. For the navigation redesign value isn’t as high.
When we run user testing there was a  little confusion about meaning of the icons
in the navigation but no other high  severity usability issues were discovered.
Adding new filters is medium value, we  received feedback from potential customers
that they can’t continue using the tool  because they can’t get the view they need.
Alright so now we’re done with assigning  Value and it’s time to asses effort.
Onboarding video is going to be quick  - almost no coding is required here
and it’ll be done fast - so it’s XS. Navigation redesign is L - in this task
we need to get design involved, we need to  carefully test designs, build new navigation
and also rewrite documentation. Adding new filters is Medium.
Now when we assigned all metrics we can  order our backlog by tasks with highest
priority and see what task is most  important to start working on first.
You can also use Priority matrix to identify quick  wins - tasks with highest value and lowest effort
And time sinks - tasks with  lowest value and highest effort.
If you’re looking for a backlog prioritization  tool that integrates with Jira where you can
use this template you can try our app Foxly. It’s really fun and easy to use and helps keep
everyone in your team and stakeholders  up to date with latest priorities.
If you feel that value versus effort  prioritization technique might not be the
right one for you and your team have a look on our  other videos where we introduce other ones like
RICE, Ice, weighted shortest  job first or quick wins method.
See you in the next video and in  the meantime And happy prioritizing  ✌️
